'''Temiri Blagg''', a [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]], was a [[Youngling|child]] who lived a forlorn existence working as a stable hand in the [[Canto Casino and Racetrack|Canto Casino]] during the [[First Order-Resistance War]].

==Biography==
[[File:Temiri-Blagg.png|thumb|300px|left|Temiri worked in the fathier stables on Cantonica.]]
Temiri Blagg was a [[Force-sensitive|Force adept]] [[Gender|boy]]<ref name="USW" /> who was part of a team of urchins—children abandoned on the [[planet]] [[Cantonica]] as a result of gambling losses—who oversaw the racing [[fathier]]s of [[Canto Bight]] under the management of [[Bargwill Tomder]].<ref name="TLJ VD">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> In [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places the events of the film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] in [[34 ABY]]. As [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']] carries on immediately from the events of ''The Force Awakens'', it can be assumed to take place in the same [[Standard year|year]].</ref> he briefly encountered the [[Resistance]] operatives [[Rose Tico]] and [[Finn]], who were attempting to evade the [[Police officer|officers]] of the [[Canto Bight Police Department]]. Finn and Tico ultimately escaped Canto Bight with the help of Blagg and his fellow urchins, who released the fathiers from the stables, resulting in the [[Species|animals]] stampeding through the [[city]] and escaping into the [[desert]].<ref name="Episode VIII" />

Following the [[Battle of Crait]], Blagg and the other stable hands listened, including [[Arashell Sar]], as another urchin, [[Oniho Zaya]], regaled them with tales of [[Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker]] and how he stood alone against the [[First Order]] on [[Crait]]. He resumed his duties shortly afterward, sweeping the floor of the stables. By then he concealed a [[Rose Tico's Resistance ring|Resistance ring]],<ref name="Episode VIII" /> a [[Galactic Civil War]]-era antique formerly owned by Tico.<ref name="TLJ VD" /> While staring at the [[star]]s, Blagg—who dreamed of a better life away from Canto Bight—[[Telekinesis|telekinetically]] lifted his broom with the [[Force power|power]] of [[the Force]].<ref name="Episode VIII" /> Blagg was later mentioned as a "young fathier stablehand" in a [[Unidentified historical book|historical text]]<ref name="100 Objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> published during or after the year [[35 ABY]].<ref name="BookDate">{{Bluesky|kristinbaver.bsky.social|post/3lxdw6e32j42a|[[Kristin Baver]]|date=2025-08-26|quote=It is! Like the visual dictionaries, Skywalker: A Family at War, and The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire, it’s part of a long line of books that are based on a construct that I adore: that the events and items in Star Wars are real.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/hodDN}} {{C|In response to: "A question, is 100 objects intended to be an in-universe book?"}} establishes that ''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]'' is supposed to be taken as an in-universe text. As the book makes reference to the events of [[35 ABY]] and dates those events as such, it must have been published in [[the galaxy]] during or after that [[Standard year|year]].</ref> The text reflected how Blagg had been given Tico's Resistance Ring.<ref name="100 Objects" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Three years today since The Last Jedi released in cinemas and Temiri Blagg was introduced to the Galaxy far far away! I love my Broom Boy character who gave the Hope to the Galaxy! To all Star Wars fans out there - May the Force always be with you!|Temirlan Blaev on Instagram|<ref>{{Instagram|username=tem_blai|url=p/CI0axG7gkIo|name=Temirlan Blaev|date=2020-12-15|quote=Three years today since The Last Jedi released in cinemas and Temiri Blagg was introduced to the Galaxy far far away! I love my Broom Boy character who gave the Hope to the Galaxy! To all Star Wars fans out there - May the Force always be with you! Thank you|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/NAcpM}}</ref>}}
Temiri Blagg first appeared in the [[2017]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']], the second film in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[sequel trilogy]] directed by [[Rian Johnson]], and was portrayed by [[Temirlan Blaev]],<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/12/17/star-wars-the-last-jedi-gives-a-name-to-that-orphan-boy|text=Star Wars: The Last Jedi gives a name to that orphan boy|author=Vejvoda, Jim|date=2017-12-17|archivedate=20220411065816}}</ref> who is listed as "Stable Boy" in the film's credits.<ref name="Episode VIII" /> The name of the character is based on the actor's name.
